description: Two records each claim to replace the same superseded record — a forked history where the spec allows exactly one line.
specRow: S9.4 NEED-DOC-001 fires on a superseded record with multiple citing supersedes (S6 rule 2).

needsDocument.title: Benefits assistance -- who this is for and why

statement.who: anyone submitting this application under a deadline
statement.want: a receipt I can save and show someone later
statement.why: if the agency loses my submission, I lose rights I actually had
statement.done: after I submit, I hold a receipt that proves what I filed and when

statement.who: anyone submitting this application under a deadline
statement.want: a receipt I can save and show someone later
statement.why: if the agency loses my submission, I lose rights I actually had
statement.done: after I submit, I hold a receipt that proves what I filed and when

statement.who: anyone submitting this application on behalf of someone else
statement.want: a receipt naming who I filed for
statement.why: without it I cannot prove I acted for the person I was helping
statement.done: after I submit, the receipt names both me and the person I filed for

note: Schema/checker divergence, and the second half of the S9.4 'zero or multiple' clause its sibling `invalid-superseded-without-successor` pins from the other end. Both successors are individually well-formed — each `supersedes` resolves to a record whose status really is `superseded` — so the defect lives only in the inverse edge's cardinality, which is a document-scope predicate JSON Schema has no keyword for. Exactly one finding fires, on the superseded record, not one per successor: the ambiguity is which line of history is the real one, and that is one defect. Both successors are adopted and cited, so no coverage code enters the verdict.
